description: We're building an interactive web app that uses radar data from the NASA-ISRO NISAR mission to track and visualize changes on Earth's surface, such as wetland loss, wildfires, earthquakes, farming activity and glacier movement. Our goal is to make complex radar data easy for anyone to explore and understand, with a clear map-based view of what is changing, where, and by how much.
summary:
ASTRAV//E – AI-Powered Earth Observation and Change Exploration Platform

ASTRAV//E is an interactive geospatial platform designed to make Earth-surface changes easier to explore, visualize, and understand using satellite-based Earth observation technologies. The project addresses the challenge of accessing and interpreting satellite data from multiple sources, particularly for monitoring environmental changes such as deforestation, floods, agricultural patterns, wetland degradation, urban expansion, and natural disasters.

The platform integrates multiple Earth-observation ecosystems, including NASA CMR, Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF), ISRO Bhoonidhi STAC API, and NASA GIBS. It leverages Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), particularly the NASA–ISRO NISAR mission's L-band and S-band capabilities, to support satellite data discovery and exploration.

Built using HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript, Leaflet.js, Node.js, Express.js, and Python, ASTRAV//E combines an interactive mapping interface with backend APIs and Python-based satellite catalogue workflows. Users can explore geographical regions, define Areas of Interest (AOIs), discover satellite datasets, and compare available imagery across different time periods.
details:
ASTRAV//E – Interactive Earth Observation & Satellite Data Exploration Platform

ASTRAV//E is an interactive geospatial platform designed to make Earth observation and satellite data more accessible, understandable, and useful. Our planet constantly experiences changes due to deforestation, urban expansion, floods, wildfires, agricultural activities, and natural disasters. However, exploring and interpreting satellite data from different sources can be complex and time-consuming.

Our project brings satellite data discovery and visualization into a unified platform. Users can explore geographical areas of interest (AOIs), discover relevant satellite datasets, and visualize Earth observation imagery through an interactive map. The platform integrates data sources and services such as NASA CMR, Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF), ISRO Bhoonidhi STAC, and NASA GIBS. It also incorporates Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and NISAR-related data discovery, helping users explore both optical and radar-based Earth observation resources.

We developed the platform using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Leaflet.js, Node.js, Express.js, and Python, along with geospatial data APIs and STAC-based workflows.

Our creativity lies in bringing multiple satellite data sources and geospatial exploration tools together through a simple, interactive interface rather than requiring users to navigate separate technical platforms.

The project's intended impact is to support students, researchers, environmental analysts, and disaster-management teams by simplifying access to Earth observation resources. Our team prioritized usability, data accessibility, integration, scalability, and the potential for future advanced SAR-based analysis and change detection.
